sentences.en: Hello, hello hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你好，你好，你好，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 推出的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: The show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 这是一个带你聆听精彩故事、了解世界上各种奇妙事物，并同时提高英语水平的节目。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today is the start of another three-part mini-series, this time on the broad theme of important scientific discovery.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们开始另一个三部分系列节目的第一集，这次的主题是重要的科学发现。

sentences.en: In part one, today’s episode, which is going to be appropriately released on February 28th, we are going to talk about the science of leap years.
sentences.zh: 在第一部分也就是今天的节目中，我们将在 2.8 这个适宜的日子里，聊聊闰年的科学。

sentences.en: In part two, we will talk about the discovery of the blueprint of life: DNA.
sentences.zh: 在第二部分，我们将谈论生命蓝图的发现：DNA。

sentences.en: And in part three we will talk about the way in which mathematics changed the world.
sentences.zh: 在第三部分，我们将讨论数学改变世界的方式。

sentences.en: OK then, let’s get right into it, and talk about leap years.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们马上切入正题，聊聊闰年。

sentences.en: Sometimes, it seems that the natural world has been created in complete harmony with mathematic principles.
sentences.zh: 有时候，自然界似乎完全遵循数学原理创造出来。

sentences.en: The Fibonacci sequence, for example, is a sequence of numbers where each new number is the sum of the previous two.
sentences.zh: 比如斐波那契数列，这是一组数字，其中每个新数字都是前两个数字的和。

sentences.en: 0,1,1,2,3,5,8,13, and so on. As any mathematician knows, the Fibonacci Sequence crops up throughout the discipline of mathematics, but it can also be found in nature, in sunflowers, pinecones, pineapples, and so on.
sentences.zh: 0、1、1、2、3、5、8、13，以此类推。正如任何数学家所知，斐波那契数列贯穿于整个数学学科，但它也能在自然界中找到，比如向日葵、松果、菠萝等等。

sentences.en: Then there’s the so-called “Golden Ratio”, a number approximately equal to 1.618, which has been called the “perfect proportion” and has often been claimed to show up in everything from the spiral of a shell to the proportions of the human body.
sentences.zh: 然后是所谓的“黄金分割率”，一个约等于 1.618 的数字，被称为“完美比例”，人们经常声称它出现在从贝壳的螺旋到人体比例的万事万物中。

sentences.en: But it’s not just in living things. Hurricane spirals, galaxies, and even the structure of DNA reflect this ratio, almost as if the universe itself is built on a foundation of mathematical elegance.
sentences.zh: 但这不仅存在于生物中。飓风螺旋、星系，甚至 DNA 的结构都反映了这个比例，几乎就像宇宙本身就是建立在数学优雅的基础之上一样。

sentences.en: But, there are some exceptions to this natural elegance.
sentences.zh: 但是，这种自然的优雅也有一些例外。

sentences.en: One example is the Earth’s orbit around the sun.
sentences.zh: 其中一个例子就是地球绕太阳的公转。

sentences.en: It takes, as we both know, 24 hours for the Earth to rotate on its axis.
sentences.zh: 我们都知道，地球自转一周需要 24 小时。

sentences.en: This is a “solar day”, the time it takes for the Sun to return to the same position in the sky, as seen from Earth.
sentences.zh: 这是一个“太阳日”，即从地球上看，太阳回到天空中同一位置所需的时间。

sentences.en: That’s simple enough, but there is a much larger problem with the Earth’s orbit, and that’s related to how long the Earth takes to go all the way around the sun.
sentences.zh: 这很简单，但地球的公转有一个更大、更复杂的问题，这与地球绕太阳转一圈需要多长时间有关。

sentences.en: Or to put it another way, the length of “a year”.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，就是“一年”的长度。

sentences.en: As we know, a year is 365 days. Apart from it isn’t exactly 365 days, it's a little bit longer than that.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所知，一年是 365 天。除了它并不完全是 365 天，它比这要长一点。

sentences.en: To be precise, it takes more like 365.2421988 days for the Earth to complete one full orbit around the sun.
sentences.zh: 准确地说，地球完成一次完整的绕日公转需要大约 365.2421988 天。

sentences.en: Or to put it in easier terms to understand, it takes 365 days and just under 6 hours.
sentences.zh: 或者用更易懂的话来说，需要 365 天加上不到 6 小时。

sentences.en: This imprecision is the reason humans created today’s topic: the leap year.
sentences.zh: 这种不精确性正是人类创造今天这个话题的原因：闰年。

sentences.en: It is a neat and tidy solution to the problem of Earth’s inexact orbit, and although on the face of it, it might seem like there’s nothing more to it than adding an extra day to February every four years, it is actually a little bit more complicated than that.
sentences.zh: 它是解决地球公转不精确问题的一个整洁利落的解决方案，虽然表面上看，这似乎只是每四年给二月增加一天那么简单，但实际上要稍微复杂一些。

sentences.en: So, to start off this exploration of the science of leap years, we need to go back to the start.
sentences.zh: 因此，要开始对闰年科学的探索，我们需要回到最初。

sentences.en: For prehistoric humans who cared little about the details of the calendar, the fact that a year wasn’t exactly 365 days was of little importance.
sentences.zh: 对于不太关心日历细节的史前人类来说，一年不正好是 365 天并不重要。

sentences.en: The sun rose in the morning and set in the evening, the moon waxed and waned, and the stars moved across the sky.
sentences.zh: 太阳日出而作、日落而息，月亮阴晴圆缺，繁星在天空中移动。

sentences.en: Those further away from the Equator had warmer seasons and colder seasons when they got more or less daylight, given the fact that the Earth is on a slight tilt.
sentences.zh: 由于地球有轻微的倾斜，离赤道较远的人们在获得或多或少的日光时，会有更温暖和更寒冷的季节。

sentences.en: Prehistoric man’s life was marked by these seasons, which would come and go on a predictable schedule - what we now call spring, summer, autumn and winter.
sentences.zh: 史前人类的生活以这些季节为标志，它们会以可预测的周期来来去去——也就是我们现在所说的春夏秋冬。

sentences.en: As humans became more settled, and civilisation started to develop, they started paying closer attention to the passage of time.
sentences.zh: 随着人类变得更加定居，文明开始发展，他们开始更加密切地关注时间的流逝。

sentences.en: Early civilisations began to notice and document patterns.
sentences.zh: 早期文明开始注意到并记录规律。

sentences.en: The Nile would flood at the same time every year, animals would migrate on a predictable schedule, and the stars would appear in the same positions at certain times.
sentences.zh: 尼罗河每年在同一时间泛滥，动物按可预测的规律迁徙，星星在特定时间出现在相同的位置。

sentences.en: It didn’t take long for people to realise that the cycle of the seasons repeated approximately every 365 days.
sentences.zh: 人们没花多久就意识到，季节的周期大约每 365 天重复一次。

sentences.en: And with this, the first calendars were born.
sentences.zh: 由此，最早的日历诞生了。

sentences.en: Many of these early calendars were, in fact, based on the moon rather than the sun.
sentences.zh: 事实上，许多早期的日历不是基于太阳，而是基于月亮。

sentences.en: A lunar cycle – the time it takes for the moon to go from one full moon to the next – is about 29.5 days.
sentences.zh: 一个农历月——月亮从一个满月到下一个满月所需的时间——大约是 29.5 天。

sentences.en: Twelve of these lunar months make up roughly 354 days, so 11 days less than a solar year, but it was near enough.
sentences.zh: 这十二个农历月构成大约 354 天，比太阳年少 11 天，但也差不多了。

sentences.en: And this was fine for a while. Many ancient civilisations, including the Babylonians and early Greeks, used lunar calendars and simply adjusted them as needed, often by adding extra months to catch up.
sentences.zh: 这样过了一段时间也挺好。许多古代文明，包括巴比伦人和早期希腊人，都使用阴历，并根据需要进行调整，通常通过增加闰月来赶上进度。

sentences.en: After all, yes there was some external trade, but so long as everyone within a particular settlement or area knew what the date was, it was relatively easy to adjust it without too much complication.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，虽然有一些对外贸易，但只要特定定居点或地区内的每个人都知道日期是什么，就相对容易调整而不会有太多麻烦。

sentences.en: But as societies grew more complex, so did their need for a more precise calendar, a calendar that accurately aligned with the Earth’s orbit around the sun.
sentences.zh: 但随着社会变得越来越复杂，对更精准日历的需求也随之增加，一个能与地球绕太阳公转精确对齐的日历。

sentences.en: That calendar was, of course, the solar calendar.
sentences.zh: 这个日历当然就是太阳历。

sentences.en: And it was the Egyptians who were among the first to adopt it.
sentences.zh: 埃及人是最早采用太阳历的人之一。

sentences.en: By observing the annual flooding of the Nile and tracking the movements of the star Sirius, they estimated a year to be about 365.25 days— remarkably close to the actual solar year.
sentences.zh: 通过观察尼罗河的年度泛滥和追踪天狼星的运动，他们估计一年大约是 365.25 天——这与实际的太阳年惊人地接近。

sentences.en: Now was the question of how to divide up those days into sensible chunks.
sentences.zh: 现在的问题是如何把这些天数划分成合理的块。

sentences.en: Their calendar had 12 months of 30 days, with 5 extra days tacked on at the end of the year as a sort of annual festival.
sentences.zh: 他们的日历有 12 个月，每个月 30 天，年底额外加上 5 天作为一种年度节日。

sentences.en: This was a big improvement–after all, it is very similar to what we have today–but it wasn’t perfect.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很大的改进——毕竟，这与我们今天所拥有的非常相似——但它并不完美。

sentences.en: Over time, the slight discrepancy between 365 days and the true length of the solar year added up, causing the calendar to drift out of sync with the seasons.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，365 天与太阳年真实长度之间的微小差异累积起来，导致日历与季节逐渐脱节。

sentences.en: Fast forward to ancient Rome, the calendar was even more of a mess.
sentences.zh: 快进到古罗马，那里的日历更加一团糟。

sentences.en: The original Roman calendar had only 10 months, starting in March and ending in December.
sentences.zh: 最初的罗马历只有 10 个月，从 3 月开始，到 12 月结束。

sentences.en: The names of our modern months still reflect this: “September” comes from the Latin word for “seven” but is our 9th month of the year, “October” comes from the Latin word for “eight” but is our tenth month of the year, and it’s a similar story with “November,” and “December”, which come from the Latin words for nine, and ten.
sentences.zh: 我们现代月份的名字仍然反映了这一点：“September”源自拉丁语的“七”，但却是我们一年的第 9 个月，“October”源自拉丁语的“八”，但却是我们一年的第十个月，“November”和“December”也是类似的情况，它们分别源自拉丁语的九和十。

sentences.en: At the time, winter was not assigned official months—the period roughly covering what we now call January and February was simply considered a dead time, an unstructured gap in the calendar.
sentences.zh: 当时，冬天没有被分配官方的月份——大致涵盖我们现在所说的 1 月和 2 月的时期被简称为一个枯水期，即日历中一个非结构化的空白期。

sentences.en: In practice, this meant that the Roman calendar was an administrative nightmare, and there were long gaps where the calendar didn’t align with the seasons at all.
sentences.zh: 在实践中，这意味着罗马日历是一场行政噩梦，并且存在很长一段时间的空白期，日历根本与季节不匹配。

sentences.en: Farmers would be planting crops at the wrong times, festivals would drift across the seasons, and even military campaigns could be thrown into disarray because the calendar no longer aligned with the natural world.
sentences.zh: 农民们会在错误的时间播种作物，节日会在各个季节之间漂移，甚至军事行动也会陷入混乱，因为日历不再与自然世界保持一致。

sentences.en: To make matters worse, powerful officials exploited this confusion for their own benefit.
sentences.zh: 更糟糕的是，有权有势的官员为了自身利益利用这种混乱。

sentences.en: If extending a year or shortening it could help them stay in power or delay an opponent’s election, they would simply adjust the calendar to suit their needs.
sentences.zh: 如果延长或缩短一年能帮助他们保持权力或推迟对手的选举，他们就会简单地调整日历来满足自己的需求。

sentences.en: It was eventually expanded to 12 months, with January and February added at the start of the year.
sentences.zh: 它最终被扩展到 12 个月，在年初增加了 1 月和 2 月。

sentences.en: But it was still pretty chaotic. By the time Julius Caesar came to power, the Roman calendar had drifted so far out of sync with the solar year that seasons were arriving three months earlier than they should.
sentences.zh: 但它仍然相当混乱。当尤利乌斯·恺撒掌权时，罗马历与太阳年的偏差已经太大了，导致季节比应有的时间提前了三个月。

sentences.en: Spring festivals were being celebrated in the middle of winter, and the practical workings of Roman society were falling apart.
sentences.zh: 春季节日竟然在仲冬时节庆祝，罗马社会的实际运作正在崩溃。

sentences.en: Caesar, a man who prided himself on his organisational ability, decided this couldn’t continue.
sentences.zh: 恺撒是一个以自己的组织能力为傲的人，他决定不能任由这种情况继续下去。

sentences.en: In 46 BCE, with the help of Greek astronomers, he reformed the calendar entirely.
sentences.zh: 公元前 46 年，在希腊天文学家的帮助下，他彻底改革了日历。

sentences.en: The Julian calendar, as it came to be known, was based on the solar year, with a length of 365.25 days.
sentences.zh: 后来被称为儒略历的日历是以太阳年为基础的，长度为 365.25 天。

sentences.en: To account for that extra 0.25 days each year, Caesar introduced the leap year, adding an extra day to February every four years.
sentences.zh: 为了说明每年多出的 0.25 天，恺撒引入了闰年，每四年给二月增加一天。

sentences.en: It was a simple and elegant solution, and it brought order back to the Roman world.
sentences.zh: 这是一个简单而优雅的解决方案，它给罗马世界带回了秩序。

sentences.en: No longer would festivals and planting seasons drift aimlessly through the year.
sentences.zh: 节日和播种季节将不再漫无目的地在一年中漂移。

sentences.en: The calendar was now tied to the cycles of the Sun.
sentences.zh: 日历现在与太阳的周期绑定在了一起。

sentences.en: But there was a small problem with Caesar’s calculations.
sentences.zh: 但恺撒的计算有一个小问题。

sentences.en: The solar year isn’t actually 365.25 days long—it’s 365.2421988 days.
sentences.zh: 太阳年的长度实际上并不是 365.25 天——而是 365.2421988 天。

sentences.en: That difference of about 11 minutes per year might seem tiny, but over time, it added up.
sentences.zh: 每年大约 11 分钟的差异看起来可能微不足道，但随着时间的推移，它累积了起来。

sentences.en: By the 16th century, the calendar had drifted out of alignment with the seasons once again.
sentences.zh: 到了 16 世纪，日历再次与季节失去了同步。

sentences.en: This time, it was Pope Gregory XIII who decided to fix the problem.
sentences.zh: 这一次，是教皇格里高利十三世决定解决这个问题。

sentences.en: In 1582, Pope Gregory introduced a new calendar, which we now call the Gregorian calendar.
sentences.zh: 在 1582 年，格里高利教皇引入了一种新日历，也就是我们现在所说的格里高利历（公历）。

sentences.en: To correct the drift, 10 days were skipped that year.
sentences.zh: 为了纠正偏差，那一年跳过了 10 天。

sentences.en: People in Catholic countries went to bed on the 4th of October and woke up on the 15th of October.
sentences.zh: 天主教国家的人们在 10 月 4 日上床睡觉，醒来时已经是 10 月 15 日了。

sentences.en: If you search for great events that happened in France, Italy, or Spain on the 5th or the 6th or the 7th of October, 1582, there were none because those days didn’t happen.
sentences.zh: 如果你搜索在 1582 年 10 月 5 日、6 日或 7 日在法国、意大利或西班牙发生过什么伟大的事件，答案是没有，因为那些日子根本没有发生。

sentences.en: Gregory also introduced a new rule to refine leap years.
sentences.zh: 格里高利还引入了一条新规则来完善闰年。

sentences.en: Under the Gregorian system, a year would only be a leap year if it was divisible by 4, but century years, like 1800 or 1900, wouldn’t be leap years unless they were also divisible by 400.
sentences.zh: 在格里高利历系统下，只有能被 4 整除的年份才是闰年，但是世纪年，比如 1800 年或 1900 年，除非它们也能被 400 整除，否则就不是闰年。

sentences.en: That’s why the year 2000, as you may remember, and the year 1600, which you will not remember, were leap years; they can be divided by 400.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么 2000 年（你可能还记得）和 1600 年（你肯定不记得）是闰年；它们可以被 400 整除。

sentences.en: And the year 2096 will be a leap year, but the year 2100 will not be a leap year because you can’t divide 2100 by 400.
sentences.zh: 2096 年将是闰年，但 2100 年将不是闰年，因为 2100 不能被 400 整除。

sentences.en: Anyway, this refinement brought the calendar back in line with the solar year and solved the 11-minute-per-year drift problem for good—or at least, for the foreseeable future.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，这种改进使日历重新与太阳年保持一致，并一劳永逸地解决了每年 11 分钟的偏差问题——或者至少在可预见的未来是这样。

sentences.en: Even so, adopting the Gregorian calendar wasn’t a smooth process.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，采用格里高利历并不是一个顺畅的过程。

sentences.en: Protestant countries were suspicious of this decidedly Catholic reform and refused to adopt it at first.
sentences.zh: 新教国家对这种绝对是天主教的改革持怀疑态度，起初拒绝采用它。

sentences.en: England and its colonies didn’t make the switch until 1752.
sentences.zh: 英国及其殖民地直到 1752 年才做出改变。

sentences.en: By then, the Julian calendar was 11 days out of sync with the Gregorian calendar, so those 11 days had to be skipped.
sentences.zh: 到那时，儒略历与格里高利历已经相差 11 天，因此必须跳过这 11 天。

sentences.en: Just as people in Catholic countries did in October 1582, in 1752, anyone living in the British Empire went to bed on September the 2nd and woke up on September the 14th.
sentences.zh: 正如天主教国家的人们在 1582 年 10 月所做的那样，在 1752 年，任何生活在大英帝国的人都在 9 月 2 日上床睡觉，醒来时已经是 9 月 14 日了。

sentences.en: It caused confusion, frustration, and even protests, but eventually, the Gregorian calendar became the global standard.
sentences.zh: 它引起了混乱、沮丧甚至抗议，但最终，格里高利历成为了全球标准。

sentences.en: Although other calendars are used, often for cultural or religious purposes, the Gregorian calendar is the most widely used civil calendar across the world today.
sentences.zh: 虽然人们也使用其他日历（通常出于文化或宗教目的），但格里高利历是当今世界各地应用最广泛的民用日历。

sentences.en: But it’s perhaps worth asking: is the Gregorian calendar the final word on how we measure time?
sentences.zh: 但也许值得一问的是：格里高利历是关于我们如何测量时间的最终定论吗？

sentences.en: Could there be better ways to organise our year, and solve the problem of leap years for good?
sentences.zh: 有没有更好的方法来组织我们的一年，并一劳永逸地解决闰年的问题？

sentences.en: Calendar reform is not just a historical curiosity—it’s a topic that continues to fascinate astronomers, mathematicians, and even policymakers.
sentences.zh: 日历改革不仅仅是一个历史古董——它是一个继续令天文学家、数学家甚至政策制定者着迷的话题。

sentences.en: So, before we go, let’s talk briefly about some of these ideas.
sentences.zh: 所以，在我们离开之前，让我们简要谈谈其中一些想法。

sentences.en: One of the more radical ideas is the concept of a perpetual calendar, where every year would follow exactly the same pattern.
sentences.zh: 其中一个比较激进的想法是永久历的概念，即每一年都遵循完全相同的模式。

sentences.en: In such a system, each date would always fall on the same day of the week, making planning simpler.
sentences.zh: 在这样的系统中，每个日期总是落在星期的同一天，从而使规划变得更简单。

sentences.en: For example, 1 January would always be a Monday.
sentences.zh: 例如，1 月 1 日总是星期一。

sentences.en: One version of this is something called The International Fixed Calendar, which was proposed in the early 20th century.
sentences.zh: 其中一个版本被称为国际固定历，这是在 20 世纪初提出的。

sentences.en: Under this system, the year would be divided into 13 months of exactly 28 days each, with one or two extra days outside the calendar entirely—holidays that wouldn’t belong to any month or week.
sentences.zh: 在该系统下，一年将被划分为 13 个月，每个月正好 28 天，另外还有一到两天完全排在日历之外——这些假期不属于任何月份或星期。

sentences.en: While such a system would perhaps streamline record-keeping, you’d still need a mechanism for those extra ~0.24 days a year, and this solution isn’t really any neater than the current leap year system.
sentences.zh: 虽然这样一个系统也许能简化记录保存，但你仍然需要一个机制来处理每年大约 0.24 天的多余时间，这个解决方案其实并不比当前的闰年系统更整洁。

sentences.en: Another intriguing idea is the World Calendar, which divides the year into 12 months, but the focus is on quarters–blocks of three months–rather than individual months.
sentences.zh: 另一个有趣的观点是世界日历，它将一年划分为 12 个月，但重点是季度——三个月的区块——而不是单个月份。

sentences.en: Each quarter would contain three months: two months with 30 days and one with 31 days.
sentences.zh: 每个季度包含三个月：两个 30 天的月份和一个 31 天的月份。

sentences.en: This consistent quarterly structure would make the calendar predictable, and an extra day—a year-end holiday outside the regular calendar—would be added to balance the total.
sentences.zh: 这种一致的季度结构将使日历具有可预测性，并且会增加额外的一天——一个位于常规日历之外的年终假期——来平衡总量。

sentences.en: Leap years would include one more extra day, often called a “leap day,” similarly placed outside the calendar structure.
sentences.zh: 闰年将包括另一个额外的一天，通常被称为“闰日”，同样放置在日历结构之外。

sentences.en: This system would retain the 12-month format we’re familiar with but introduce regularity and symmetry within the year.
sentences.zh: 这个系统将保留我们熟悉的 12 个月格式，但在一年内引入了规律性和对称性。

sentences.en: Now, while both of these are perhaps interesting ideas, they have never gained serious traction.
sentences.zh: 现在，虽然这两个可能都是有趣的想法，但它们从未真正获得广泛认可。

sentences.en: You still have the problem of a year not being exactly 365 days, so some sort of extra days need to be added somewhere.
sentences.zh: 你仍然面临着一年不正好是 365 天的问题，因此某种额外的天数需要加在某个地方。

sentences.en: And then there’s the most ambitious idea of all: changing the speed of the Earth’s orbit around the sun.
sentences.zh: 还有最宏伟的想法：改变地球绕太阳公转的速度。

sentences.en: If the Earth’s orbit around the Sun could be adjusted so that it took exactly 365 days, rather than just over 365 days, we wouldn’t need leap years at all, and we could keep the same calendar system.
sentences.zh: 如果能调整地球绕太阳的公转速度，使其刚好花费 365 天，而不是刚好超过 365 天，我们就根本不需要闰年，并且可以保持相同的日历系统不变。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, this is impossible, with today’s technology at least.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，至少以当今的技术来看，这是不可能的。

sentences.en: The Earth’s orbit is governed by the gravitational pull of the Sun and the balance between that pull and the planet’s velocity.
sentences.zh: 地球的公转受太阳引力以及该引力与行星速度之间的平衡所支配。

sentences.en: To change the speed of the Earth’s orbit, we would need to either increase or decrease its velocity significantly.
sentences.zh: 要改变地球公转的速度，我们需要大幅增加或减少其速度。

sentences.en: This would require an unimaginable amount of energy—far beyond what humanity could ever generate.
sentences.zh: 这将需要难以想象的巨大能量——远远超过人类所能产生的能量。

sentences.en: And even if it were possible, the unintended consequences could be catastrophic.
sentences.zh: 即使这是可能的，意想不到的后果也可能是灾难性的。

sentences.en: Changing the speed of the Earth’s orbit would affect the gravitational balance of the entire solar system, potentially destabilising the orbits of other planets and moons.
sentences.zh: 改变地球公转速度会影响整个太阳系的引力平衡，可能破坏其他行星和卫星轨道的稳定。

sentences.en: It could even disrupt the delicate conditions that make life on Earth possible, such as our climate and the length of the seasons.
sentences.zh: 它甚至可能破坏使地球生命成为可能的微妙条件，例如我们的气候和季节的长度。

sentences.en: It’s an interesting thought experiment but not one that’s grounded in reality.
sentences.zh: 这是一个有趣的思维实验，但并不扎根于现实。

sentences.en: What’s more, it’s not really necessary. Leap years aren’t so bad at all, and the Gregorian calendar and its cunning system of calculating which years to add extra days to, while imperfect, is a pretty clever solution.
sentences.zh: 更何况，这其实没有必要。闰年一点也不糟糕，格里高利历及其计算在哪一年增加额外日子的狡猾系统，虽然不完美，却是一个相当聪明的解决方案。

sentences.en: Could it be improved? Perhaps. But there really is very little need to do so.
sentences.zh: 它可以改进吗？也许可以。但真的没有太大必要这样做。

sentences.en: Sometimes, the systems we inherit endure not because they are perfect but because they work well enough.
sentences.zh: 有时候，我们继承的系统之所以能够存续，不是因为它们完美，而是因为它们足够好用。

sentences.en: So, to wrap things up, today, we hardly need to think about leap years.
sentences.zh: 所以，总而言之，今天我们几乎不需要考虑闰年。

sentences.en: They’re a part of life, quietly keeping our calendars in sync with the seasons.
sentences.zh: 它们是生活的一部分，默默地让我们的日历与季节保持同步。

sentences.en: But when you stop to consider them, they’re an incredible testament to human ingenuity.
sentences.zh: 但当你停下来思考它们时，它们是人类创造力的不可思议的证明。

sentences.en: They show how, even thousands of years ago, we were observing, calculating, and innovating to make sense of the universe.
sentences.zh: 它们展示了即使在几千年前，我们是如何通过观察、计算和创新来理解宇宙的。

sentences.en: And they remind us that while the natural world may not be perfectly elegant, our ability to adapt and find solutions is something truly remarkable.
sentences.zh: 它们提醒我们，虽然自然界可能并不完全优雅，但我们适应和寻找解决方案的能力确实非常了不起。

sentences.en: OK then, that is it for today's episode on the science of leap years.
sentences.zh: 好了，今天的关于闰年科学的节目就到这里。

sentences.en: I hope it's been an interesting one, and that you've learnt something new.
sentences.zh: 希望这是一期有趣的节目，并且让你学到了新东西。

sentences.en: As always, I would love to know what you thought about this episode.
sentences.zh: 和往常一样，我很想知道你对这期节目的看法。

sentences.en: You can head right into our community forum, which is at community.leonardoenglish.com and get chatting away to other curious minds.
sentences.zh: 你可以直接进入我们的社区论坛，网址是 community.leonardoenglish.com，与其他好奇的心灵畅聊。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你收听的是由 Leonardo English 推出的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，请注意安全，我们下期节目见。
